covers.desc: Why computers can't store most real numbers exactly, and identifying overflow and underflow in a floating-point system.
Be able to convert between bits, bytes, and larger storage units
Be able to identify the sign, significand, and exponent of a floating-point number and determine whether a value is representable given a system's (beta, p, m, M) parameters.
Be able to describe the IEEE 754 single- and double-precision bit layouts and how bits are split among sign, significand, and exponent.
Be able to compute machine epsilon for a floating-point system and use it to bound the worst-case relative error of a stored value.
